why: secretKey[i] % param[i] can be any residue in [0, param[i]-1], so each parameter picks one value from 0..param[i]-1 and you want as many distinct picks as possible. Sorting the bounds and handing each the smallest unused value is the classic greedy assignment.
hints: Forget the secret key: what set of values can hash[i] take for a given param[i]?
Each index may claim any value in [0, param[i]-1]. Process small bounds first, because they have the fewest options, and give each the next new value 0, 1, 2, ... if its bound allows it.
Sort param; keep a counter cur of distinct values used; for each p, if cur < p then cur += 1. Answer is cur. O(n log n).
pitfalls: param[i] = 1 forces hash[i] = 0, so many 1s still contribute only one distinct value.
Do not try to build actual keys; values up to 10^9 make that pointless, only the residue range matters.
